...RESPONDENTS (BY SRI.MANJUNATH K., HCGP FOR RESPONDENTS)
 THIS WRIT PETITION IS FILED UNDER ARTICLES 226 AND 227 OF THE CONSTITUTION OF INDIA PRAYING TO THE RESPONDENT TO GRANT OF EMERGENCY PAROLE FOR A PERIOD OF 30 DAYS SO AS TO ENABLE THE PETITIONER TO ATTEND THE OBSEQUIES CEREMONY OF HIS FATHER AS PER THE KARNATAKA PRISONS RULES PRODUCED AS ANNX-E.
 THIS WRIT PETITION, COMING ON FOR PRELIMINARY HEARING, THIS DAY, THE COURT MADE THE FOLLOWING:
 ORDER

The petitioner is before this Court seeking a direction by issuance of a writ in the nature of mandamus to respondents granting emergency parole for a period of 30 days, to enable the petitioner to attend the obsequies ceremony of his father.
2.
Heard Sri K.B.Monesh Kumar, learned counsel for the petitioner and the learned High Court Government Pleader for the respondent - State.
3. The petitioner gets embroiled in a crime registered for the offence under Section 498A and 302 of the IPC and was NC: 2023:KHC:40665 taken into custody on 09.08.2012.
He has remained in custody since then.
The imprisonment certificate dated 31.10.2023, would indicate that the petitioner has now completed total sentence of 13 years, 2 months and 22 days including remission.
The certificate would further indicate that the petitioner has not sought for parole from the date of his imprisonment.
It is for the first time, the petitioner has knocked at the doors of this Court seeking his release on emergency parole on account of performing obsequies on the death of his father.
The death certificate indicates that the father of the petitioner died on 26.10.2023.
4. In the light of the death of his father, the petitioner would become entitled to grant of emergency parole for a period of 30 days from 16.11.2023 to 15.12.2023.

5. For the aforesaid reasons, the following:

2 (i) The Writ Petition is allowed.

sentences.text: (ii) Mandamus issues respondents 2 and 3 to consider the representation of the petitioner and release the NC: 2023:KHC:40665 detenue/Nawaj (convict Prisoner No.7506) on emergency parole for 30 days, from the forenoon of 16.11.2023, till the evening of 15.12.2023.

(iii) The respondents 2 and 3 shall stipulate strict conditions as are usually stipulated, to ensure return of the detenue to the gaol and that he shall not commit any other offence during the period of parole.
(iv) Registry is directed to communicate this order to respondent Nos.2 and 3, by way of electronic mail, forthwith.
